title: Guide
description: Explains the user's own estate — their agents, what each is built from, its trust state, and the user's usage — in words, from what the platform returns.

examples.outcome: It reads the agent's trust state and what decides it, then explains in words which ingredient changed and what you would sign. It never signs.

examples.ask: What is @SALES and what does it use?
examples.outcome: One call to the agent's overview: its class, model, data source, repositories, experts, components, skills and trust state, summarised.
It counts what is unacknowledged in your Assurance Inbox and what waits in your review queue, and tells you where to act. It acknowledges nothing.

examples.ask: How much have I used this period?
examples.outcome: It reads your usage and warnings and says where you stand against your limits.

not_offered.what: Any change — to an agent, a repository, a flow or a schedule
not_offered.why: The Guide only explains. Changes belong to the Agent Builder, the Knowledge Curator and the Automation Builder — or to you.

not_offered.what: Signing anything, attesting a deployment, or withdrawing a signature
not_offered.why: A signature is your statement that you checked it. An agent signing — or unsigning — its own work proves nothing.

not_offered.what: Opening an agent to the REST API, or making one your default
not_offered.why: They decide what every other client and conversation runs on.

not_offered.what: Other users' usage, conversations or unattributed signatures
not_offered.why: An agent works on your items only — even when your tier lets you see more. Giving a signature to another account is an administrator's act.
